lessons.name: Flat / long crosser
lessons.understand: A target travelling predominantly across the shooter's view. Distance can make the picture deceptive, so the lesson separates reading the line and speed from consciously measuring a lead gap.

coaching.text: Pull-away, swing-through and maintained lead are recognised CPSA methods; ShotSight presents them as options rather than one universal answer.
coaching.label: DIRECT

coaching.text: For a long crosser, Don Currie/NSCA teaches a pull-away protocol built around a useful runway, leading-edge focus, speed match and smooth separation.
coaching.label: DIRECT

coaching.text: Checking or measuring lead can draw attention away from the target and is a plausible contributor when the shooter repeatedly finishes behind.
coaching.label: DIRECT

holds: Do not claim maintained lead is always best when the target is visible early.
Do not state a specific left/right body-rotation cause without evidence.

candidate_mechanisms: loss of target focus through lead checking
diagnose.question: Can you track the same target smoothly without firing, while keeping visual attention on the target?
diagnose.interpretation: If the no-shot trace is smooth but the live trace deteriorates near the trigger, execution becomes more likely; otherwise retain reading/connection alternatives.
diagnose.fix: Repeat one method with a fixed break zone, then compare methods without scoring a 'correct lead'.
diagnose.retest: Change speed or distance while retaining the same method.

visual_spec.warning: Blue gun line is conceptual; no exact ballistic lead claim.

lessons.name: Quartering away
lessons.understand: A target moving both across and away. The important first task is to classify the actual angle rather than treating every quarterer as a crosser or a straight going-away bird.

coaching.text: CPSA coaching explicitly cautions against rushing the quartering-away target and emphasises smooth, consistent execution.
coaching.label: DIRECT

coaching.text: OSP teaches its own early-move quartering approach; keep it attributed rather than presenting it as universal.
coaching.label: DIRECT

coaching.text: For fast quarterers repeatedly missed behind, Don Currie describes a specific quartering/come-to-gun solution with defined hold and visual pickup.
coaching.label: DIRECT

holds: Do not claim a universal perceptual 'speed compression' rule drives technique.

candidate_mechanisms: method not matched to this presentation
diagnose.question: Does the miss persist when the same speed is presented at a more crossing angle?
diagnose.interpretation: A change with angle increases the probability of classification/path error rather than a generic gun-speed fault.
diagnose.fix: Use a blocked angle comparison before randomising angles.
diagnose.retest: Novel quartering angle in both directions.

visual_spec.warning: Do not convert the schematic into an exact lead value.

lessons.name: Low fast incomer / cutoff
lessons.understand: This lesson is for an incoming/quartering target that transitions, drops or cuts near the chosen break zone. A plain straight incomer must not inherit this method automatically.

coaching.text: Don Currie's cutoff presentation matches a low incoming/quartering target that changes near the break point and supports an offset/closer hold with a slightly upward approach that preserves target visibility.
coaching.label: DIRECT

coaching.text: Josh Brown/TGS/ShotKam separately supports explicit pickup, hold and kill-point planning on incomers and keeping the gun below a descending target.
coaching.label: DIRECT

holds: Do not prescribe a late intercept from below for every low fast incomer.

candidate_mechanisms: following early line instead of final transition
diagnose.question: If the target is replayed without the final drop/cut, does the error remain?
diagnose.interpretation: Improvement when the transition is removed points toward transition reading/approach rather than a generic incomer problem.
diagnose.fix: Rehearse the final useful line and preserve target visibility.
diagnose.retest: Randomise the direction/amount of the late cut.

visual_spec.warning: Component toggles are a ShotSight experimental diagnostic, not established proof.

lessons.name: Chandelle / looper around apex
lessons.understand: A curved target whose rising, apex and descending phases are materially different tasks. The page requires the shooter to choose or identify the intended break phase.

coaching.text: Don Currie/NSCA teaches committing to a break point, focusing on the leading edge, matching gun and target speed and avoiding tracing the whole arc.
coaching.label: DIRECT

coaching.text: For a descending break point, an upward/offset approach can preserve visibility rather than letting the muzzle occlude the target.
coaching.label: DIRECT

coaching.text: ShotSight therefore treats rise, apex and descent as separate phases instead of one generic looper technique.
coaching.label: SYNTHESIS

diagnose.symptom: misses underneath or loses the clay near the top
diagnose.question: Which phase are you actually trying to break: rising, apex or descending?
diagnose.interpretation: If the answer is unclear, classification/break-point planning precedes a technique prescription.
diagnose.fix: Choose one phase and rehearse the target path to that break zone only.
diagnose.retest: Move the break zone to a different phase.

visual_spec.warning: No fixed millisecond apex threshold; any timing ladder is experimental.

lessons.name: Rising teal — under power
lessons.understand: A rising/outgoing teal that must be engaged while it is still travelling under power. This is intentionally distinct from a near-apex teal.

coaching.text: Don Currie/NSCA explicitly distinguishes a comfortable near-peak teal from an outgoing teal that must be shot under power.
coaching.label: DIRECT

coaching.text: For the outgoing-under-power case, Currie teaches a pass-through move with a hold point about one-third back from the break point.
coaching.label: DIRECT

coaching.text: Other respected coaching can favour an apex or rise solution in different teal contexts; ShotSight must preserve that disagreement rather than declaring one universal teal method.
coaching.label: SYNTHESIS

holds: Apex is not universally the best place to shoot a teal.

diagnose.symptom: misses above/below or timing changes wildly
candidate_mechanisms: gun speed not adapting to target deceleration
diagnose.question: Are you shooting it under power or near the peak?
diagnose.interpretation: A phase mismatch invalidates a one-size technique diagnosis.
diagnose.fix: Train one phase at a time before mixing phases.
diagnose.retest: Change only the break phase, then add drift.

visual_spec.target: steep rising path with optional lateral drift
visual_spec.warning: Hidden-drift scoring/gearbox metrics are experimental ShotSight hypotheses.

lessons.name: Crossing rabbit
lessons.understand: A rabbit is not merely a low crosser. Ground proximity, rolling/bouncing behaviour and presentation angle affect perception and method; crossing, shallow-quartering and slow/close rabbits are separate variants.

coaching.text: Don Currie notes that ground proximity can make a rabbit appear faster and identifies a common tendency to miss in front.
coaching.label: DIRECT

coaching.text: For a crossing rabbit, Currie teaches a specific let-it-beat-the-muzzle then move-to-the-nose/front-foot method, while slow or quartering rabbits can use different approaches.
coaching.label: DIRECT

holds: Do not teach 'ignore every bounce and shoot the average line' as established fact.
Do not list pull-away/maintained/swing-through as universally valid rabbit options.

candidate_mechanisms: reacting to bounce instead of target information
diagnose.question: Is this a broad crossing rabbit, a shallow quarterer, or a slow/close rabbit?
diagnose.interpretation: Method advice follows the actual variant; the label 'rabbit' alone is insufficient.
diagnose.fix: Classify the presentation first, then use the source-matched method.

visual_spec.warning: Do not imply Project can reproduce live ground physics exactly.

lessons.name: Driven incoming target
lessons.understand: A true driven target is incoming from height and may pass overhead. ShotSight keeps it separate from a target already passing overhead and travelling away.

coaching.text: Don Currie/NSCA teaches a pass-through/swing-through driven-target method with visual connection before the pass-through move.
coaching.label: DIRECT

coaching.text: Across expert overhead/driven instruction, timed mount/connection followed by controlled separation is a defensible synthesis, but exact language and method depend on the incoming-versus-passing geometry.
coaching.label: SYNTHESIS

holds: Do not state that pull-away or maintained lead is preferred on all overhead targets.

diagnose.symptom: stab/poke, late loss of target, or behind high
diagnose.question: Are you breaking the target while it is still incoming, or after it has passed and is going away?
diagnose.interpretation: A passing-away overhead is a different task and should route to a different play.
diagnose.fix: Use geometry-matched no-shot tracking and preserve visual connection before prescribing a live method.
diagnose.retest: Lower driven version, then true overhead/passing comparison.

visual_spec.warning: A wall projector cannot reproduce true depth; label this as conceptual 2D rehearsal.

lessons.name: On-report / true-pair planning
lessons.understand: Pairs are sequence contexts, not one target geometry. Each bird is classified independently, then ShotSight adds order, break-point and transition planning.

coaching.text: CPSA explicitly demonstrates using different shooting methods within pairs.
coaching.label: DIRECT

coaching.text: CPSA also highlights first-shot timing as a way of improving the setup for the second target in simultaneous-pair examples.
coaching.label: DIRECT

coaching.text: Don Currie/NSCA teaches planning true-pair order from break-point geometry, visibility/time window and transition route.
coaching.label: DIRECT

holds: Following, report, simultaneous/true and rafale are not interchangeable terms.
Exact transition-latency thresholds are not validated.

diagnose.symptom: second bird repeatedly lost or rushed
candidate_mechanisms: first target finished too late for available second-bird window
attention leaves first target too early
diagnose.question: What pair type is it, and where are both intended break points?
diagnose.interpretation: Without pair definition and both target geometries, no reliable pair diagnosis should be issued.
diagnose.fix: Plan both birds explicitly, then vary only the transition constraint.
diagnose.retest: Reverse target order or change second-bird window where the format allows.

visual_spec.warning: Attention metrics and transition thresholds remain experimental ShotSight hypotheses.
